documents.title: Suitability report - March 2025
documents.content:
Suitability report prepared for Mrs Margaret Ashworth by Hannah Price, Chartered Financial Planner, Nevis Wealth. Date: 17 March 2025.
1. Why you came to us. Following the death of your husband Geoffrey, you inherited £684,300 from his estate, which is currently held in a building society account earning a variable rate of interest. You asked us how to invest this money so that it produces a reliable income to top up your NHS pension, while keeping some cash available for emergencies and for helping your grandchildren.
2. Your circumstances. You are 72, in good health, and own your home in Harrogate outright. Your pension income is about £38,000 a year before tax and covers your regular spending. You have no debts. Your son Jonathan holds a registered lasting power of attorney but you continue to manage your own affairs.
3. Your attitude to risk. You completed our attitude to risk questionnaire on 4 February 2025 and scored 3 on our scale of 1 to 7, which we describe as Cautious. We discussed the result and you agreed it reflects how you feel about investment losses. Your capacity for loss is moderate: a fall in value would not affect your standard of living, because your pension covers your essential spending.
4. Our recommendation. We recommend that you invest £600,000 in our Cautious Income Portfolio through an ISA (£20,000 this tax year) and a general investment account, and keep £84,300 in an easy-access savings account. The portfolio aims to produce a natural income of around £21,000 a year, paid monthly to your current account, without drawing on capital. We will use your ISA allowance each April to move money gradually into the tax-free wrapper.
5. Why this is suitable. The recommendation meets your objective of a regular income, matches your Cautious risk profile, and keeps enough cash for your plans. We considered leaving the money on deposit but inflation would erode its value over time.
6. Costs. Initial advice fee 1% (£6,000). Ongoing advice fee 0.5% a year, platform charge 0.15% a year and average fund charges of 0.22% a year.
7. Risks. The value of investments and the income from them can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you invest. Income is not guaranteed.
Please read this report carefully and contact me if anything is unclear.

documents.title: UK utilities - sector note for SIPP discussion
documents.content: Research note prepared for Jonathan Ashworth, who asked whether to add UK utility shares to his SIPP. Regulated water and energy network companies earn returns set by their regulators in five-year price reviews. Household bills are expected to rise by around 20% over the next review period, which supports revenue but brings political risk if customers struggle to pay. Dividend yields across the sector are about 5%, but several companies carry high debt. Our view: a utility infrastructure fund is a more diversified way to gain exposure than individual shares. Suggested allocation no more than 5% of the SIPP. To be discussed at the next review.

documents.title: Fact find - D Okafor (November 2024)
documents.content:
Client fact find. Completed at meeting on 12 November 2024 by Hannah Price, Nevis Wealth.
Personal details: Daniel Chukwuma Okafor, born 3 April 1971, married to Adaeze Okafor (born 1974). Two adult children, Tobi (24) and Amara (21), both financially independent. Home: The Granary, Moor Lane, Ilkley LS29 8QT, owned jointly, estimated value £1,100,000, no mortgage. Health: good, non-smoker.
Employment and income: Daniel founded Okafor Precision Engineering Ltd in 2009 and sold it on 30 September 2024. He is retained by the buyer as a consultant for 12 months at £5,000 a month. Adaeze is a self-employed interior designer earning about £35,000 a year. Expected income in 2024/25: consultancy £30,000 plus deposit interest.
Assets: Thameside Bank current and savings accounts about £4.6 million, mainly the net sale proceeds. Deferred consideration of £550,000 due in September 2026. Stocks and shares ISAs £182,000 (Daniel) and £96,000 (Adaeze). Deferred final salary pension in the Hallam Engineering Staff Pension Scheme from his earlier employment (1993-2008); a transfer value has been requested. No other pensions.
Liabilities: none.
Protection: no life cover since the company's group scheme ended at the sale.
Estate planning: Daniel and Adaeze have not made wills. We explained the risks of intestacy and that their estate is now well above the inheritance tax nil-rate bands. Referral to a solicitor agreed.
Objectives: (1) invest the sale proceeds for long-term growth while keeping £500,000 in cash; (2) consider moving to Portugal in 2025 or 2026, so they need advice on tax residency before they leave; (3) help the children buy homes; (4) decide whether to take the defined benefit pension or transfer it.
Attitude to risk: to be assessed with the questionnaire at the next meeting. Initial discussion suggests a balanced approach.
Identity and address: passport and bank statement seen; source of funds evidenced by the completion letter from Hollis Grant LLP.

documents.title: Letter from Marlow Tax LLP - 2025/26 position
documents.content:
Marlow Tax LLP, Chartered Tax Advisers, Harrogate. Our ref MT/OKA/2025/06. 20 January 2025.
Dear Mr Okafor,
You asked us whether you will still be treated as resident in the UK for tax purposes if you and Adaeze move to Portugal next summer. Under the statutory residence test you are UK resident for 2024/25 because your only home is in Ilkley and you spend most of the year here. For 2025/26, if you leave on 31 August 2025, sell or let The Granary, and spend fewer than 16 days in the UK in 2026/27, you should qualify for split-year treatment, so that you are taxed in the UK only on your worldwide income up to the date you leave. You would become resident in Portugal under its domestic rules from your arrival. The UK-Portugal double tax treaty will decide residence for the overlap period. Please be aware that the temporary non-residence rules can tax gains realised abroad if you return to the UK within five years. We suggest you do not make large disposals before you have left.
Yours sincerely,
Peter Marlow CTA

THIS DEED OF SETTLEMENT is made on 2 May 2023 between (1) THOMAS EDWARD WHITFIELD and ELEANOR JANE WHITFIELD, both of 12 Quarry Rise, Bath BA1 5TL (the Settlors) and (2) THOMAS EDWARD WHITFIELD, ELEANOR JANE WHITFIELD and MARTIN PAUL WHITFIELD (the Original Trustees).
1. Name. The settlement shall be known as the Whitfield Family Discretionary Trust.
2. Trust fund. The Settlors have transferred £10 to the Original Trustees, to be held on the trusts of this deed together with any property later added to it by the Settlors or anyone else, including under the Settlors' wills and the proceeds of any life policy written in trust for the Trustees.
3. Beneficiaries. The Beneficiaries are the children and remoter descendants of the Settlors, whether born before or after the date of this deed, the spouses and civil partners and widows and widowers of those descendants, and any charity. The Settlors and any person who has added property to the trust are excluded from benefit.
4. Trust period. The trust period ends 125 years from the date of this deed or on any earlier date the Trustees specify by deed.
5. Discretionary trusts. During the trust period the Trustees may pay or apply the income and capital of the trust fund to or for the benefit of any one or more of the Beneficiaries, in such shares and in such manner as the Trustees in their absolute discretion think fit. Income not applied within 21 years may be accumulated and added to capital.
6. Powers. The Trustees have the widest powers of investment, as if they were absolutely entitled to the trust fund, and may lend money to a Beneficiary interest-free, buy a home for a Beneficiary to occupy, and appoint investment managers and nominees.
7. Trustees. There must be at least two Trustees at all times. The power to appoint new Trustees is held by the Settlors jointly during their lives and then by the survivor.
8. Exclusion of the Settlors. No part of the trust fund may be paid or lent to, or applied for the benefit of, either Settlor in any circumstances.
9. Law. This deed is governed by the law of England and Wales.
Registered with HMRC's Trust Registration Service; unique reference number XATRUST80046612.
Signed as a deed by each of the Settlors and the Original Trustees in the presence of a witness.

queries.why: Assignment example: utility bills (d01 says 'utility bill', d16/d34/d39 do not), the council tax bill, bank statement, mortgage statement and tenancy agreement all prove address; the photocard licence shows the address and is accepted by many firms; the courier proof of delivery (d06), the chaser e-mail asking for proof of address (d35) and the change-of-address e-mail (d17) are traps.
Same need as q001 in the usual wording; only documents that evidence the client's home address count, not documents that merely mention an address.

Payslip, P60, SA302 tax calculation and the accountant's income letter evidence income; the 'income' wording in the suitability report, income fund holdings, trust deed and pension letters is a decoy.

Passport, French national identity card and photocard driving licence are photo ID; the chaser e-mail asking for photo ID (d35), the courier note mentioning a returned passport and a parcel photo (d06) and the fact find noting 'passport seen' are traps.

Inheritance distribution letter, property sale completion statement and business sale completion letter evidence how the wealth arose; the bank statement showing the sale proceeds arriving is supporting evidence; documents that only carry the firm name 'Nevis Wealth' are noise.

The tax adviser's statutory residence test letter and the CRS self-certification are about tax residence; the fact find mentions the need for residency advice; the council tax bill ('only adult resident') is a decoy.

Wills, the LPA, the trust deed and the letter of wishes are the estate planning documents; the life policy written in trust is related; the solicitor's letter about administering the late husband's estate (d03) is estate administration, not planning.

SIPP annual statement and Teachers' Pension annual benefit statement are pension statements; the CETV statement of entitlement is a pension statement of a kind; the payslip's pension deduction and the meeting note asking Eleanor to find her statement are not.
Both Harbourside life policies and the Tamarisk critical illness policy are protection policies; meeting notes and the fact find only discuss cover.
The three e-mail documents; scanned letters are correspondence but not e-mails, and client records with an e-mail field are not what is asked for.
In onboarding 'proof of residence' means proof of address; because the phrase can also be read as tax residence, the residence letter and self-certification are acceptable.
